GoogleIamV1Policy.description: An Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy, which specifies access controls for Google Cloud resources. A `Policy` is a collection of `bindings`. A `binding` binds one or more `members`, or principals, to a single `role`. Principals can be user accounts, service accounts, Google groups, and domains (such as G Suite). A `role` is a named list of permissions; each `role` can be an IAM predefined role or a user-created custom role. For some types of Google Cloud resources, a `binding` can also specify a `condition`, which is a logical expression that allows access to a resource only if the expression evaluates to `true`. A condition can add constraints based on attributes of the request, the resource, or both. To learn which resources support conditions in their IAM policies, see the [IAM documentation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/help/conditions/resource-policies). **JSON example:** ``` { "bindings": [ { "role": "roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin", "members": [ "user:mike@example.com", "group:admins@example.com", "domain:google.com", "serviceAccount:my-project-id@appspot.gserviceaccount.com" ] }, { "role": "roles/resourcemanager.organizationViewer", "members": [ "user:eve@example.com" ], "condition": { "title": "expirable access", "description": "Does not grant access after Sep 2020", "expression": "request.time < timestamp('2020-10-01T00:00:00.000Z')", } } ], "etag": "BwWWja0YfJA=", "version": 3 } ``` **YAML example:** ``` bindings: - members: - user:mike@example.com - group:admins@example.com - domain:google.com - serviceAccount:my-project-id@appspot.gserviceaccount.com role: roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin - members: - user:eve@example.com role: roles/resourcemanager.organizationViewer condition: title: expirable access description: Does not grant access after Sep 2020 expression: request.time < timestamp('2020-10-01T00:00:00.000Z') etag: BwWWja0YfJA= version: 3 ``` For a description of IAM and its features, see the [IAM documentation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/).

version.description: Specifies the format of the policy. Valid values are `0`, `1`, and `3`. Requests that specify an invalid value are rejected. Any operation that affects conditional role bindings must specify version `3`. This requirement applies to the following operations: * Getting a policy that includes a conditional role binding * Adding a conditional role binding to a policy * Changing a conditional role binding in a policy * Removing any role binding, with or without a condition, from a policy that includes conditions **Important:** If you use IAM Conditions, you must include the `etag` field whenever you call `setIamPolicy`. If you omit this field, then IAM allows you to overwrite a version `3` policy with a version `1` policy, and all of the conditions in the version `3` policy are lost. If a policy does not include any conditions, operations on that policy may specify any valid version or leave the field unset. To learn which resources support conditions in their IAM policies, see the [IAM documentation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/help/conditions/resource-policies).

bindings.description: Associates a list of `members`, or principals, with a `role`. Optionally, may specify a `condition` that determines how and when the `bindings` are applied. Each of the `bindings` must contain at least one principal. The `bindings` in a `Policy` can refer to up to 1,500 principals; up to 250 of these principals can be Google groups. Each occurrence of a principal counts towards these limits. For example, if the `bindings` grant 50 different roles to `user:alice@example.com`, and not to any other principal, then you can add another 1,450 principals to the `bindings` in the `Policy`.

etag.description: `etag` is used for optimistic concurrency control as a way to help prevent simultaneous updates of a policy from overwriting each other. It is strongly suggested that systems make use of the `etag` in the read-modify-write cycle to perform policy updates in order to avoid race conditions: An `etag` is returned in the response to `getIamPolicy`, and systems are expected to put that etag in the request to `setIamPolicy` to ensure that their change will be applied to the same version of the policy. **Important:** If you use IAM Conditions, you must include the `etag` field whenever you call `setIamPolicy`. If you omit this field, then IAM allows you to overwrite a version `3` policy with a version `1` policy, and all of the conditions in the version `3` policy are lost.

This field corresponds to the `ports` field of the Kubernetes Containers [v1 core API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.23/#container-v1-core).

This URI must identify an image in Artifact Registry or Container Registry. Learn more about the [container publishing requirements](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#publishing), including permissions requirements for the Vertex AI Service Agent. The container image is ingested upon ModelService.UploadModel, stored internally, and this original path is afterwards not used. To learn about the requirements for the Docker image itself, see [Custom container requirements](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#). You can use the URI to one of Vertex AI's [pre-built container images for prediction](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/pre-built-containers) in this field.

Vertex AI also sends liveness and health checks to this port. If you do not specify this field, gRPC requests to the container will be disabled. Vertex AI does not use ports other than the first one listed. This field corresponds to the `ports` field of the Kubernetes Containers v1 core API.

healthRoute.description: Immutable. HTTP path on the container to send health checks to. Vertex AI intermittently sends GET requests to this path on the container's IP address and port to check that the container is healthy. Read more about [health checks](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#health). For example, if you set this field to `/bar`, then Vertex AI intermittently sends a GET request to the `/bar` path on the port of your container specified by the first value of this `ModelContainerSpec`'s ports field. If you don't specify this field, it defaults to the following value when you deploy this Model to an Endpoint: /v1/endpoints/ENDPOINT/deployedModels/ DEPLOYED_MODEL:predict The placeholders in this value are replaced as follows: * ENDPOINT: The last segment (following `endpoints/`)of the Endpoint.name][] field of the Endpoint where this Model has been deployed. (Vertex AI makes this value available to your container code as the [`AIP_ENDPOINT_ID` environment variable](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#aip-variables).) * DEPLOYED_MODEL: DeployedModel.id of the `DeployedModel`. (Vertex AI makes this value available to your container code as the [`AIP_DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID` environment variable](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#aip-variables).)

command.description: Immutable. Specifies the command that runs when the container starts. This overrides the container's [ENTRYPOINT](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#entrypoint). Specify this field as an array of executable and arguments, similar to a Docker `ENTRYPOINT`'s "exec" form, not its "shell" form. If you do not specify this field, then the container's `ENTRYPOINT` runs, in conjunction with the args field or the container's [`CMD`](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#cmd), if either exists. If this field is not specified and the container does not have an `ENTRYPOINT`, then refer to the Docker documentation about [how `CMD` and `ENTRYPOINT` interact](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#understand-how-cmd-and-entrypoint-interact). If you specify this field, then you can also specify the `args` field to provide additional arguments for this command. However, if you specify this field, then the container's `CMD` is ignored. See the [Kubernetes documentation about how the `command` and `args` fields interact with a container's `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/inject-data-application/define-command-argument-container/#notes). In this field, you can reference [environment variables set by Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#aip-variables) and environment variables set in the env field. You cannot reference environment variables set in the Docker image. In order for environment variables to be expanded, reference them by using the following syntax: $( VARIABLE_NAME) Note that this differs from Bash variable expansion, which does not use parentheses. If a variable cannot be resolved, the reference in the input string is used unchanged. To avoid variable expansion, you can escape this syntax with `$$`; for example: $$(VARIABLE_NAME) This field corresponds to the `command` field of the Kubernetes Containers [v1 core API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.23/#container-v1-core).

predictRoute.description: Immutable. HTTP path on the container to send prediction requests to. Vertex AI forwards requests sent using projects.locations.endpoints.predict to this path on the container's IP address and port. Vertex AI then returns the container's response in the API response. For example, if you set this field to `/foo`, then when Vertex AI receives a prediction request, it forwards the request body in a POST request to the `/foo` path on the port of your container specified by the first value of this `ModelContainerSpec`'s ports field. If you don't specify this field, it defaults to the following value when you deploy this Model to an Endpoint: /v1/endpoints/ENDPOINT/deployedModels/DEPLOYED_MODEL:predict The placeholders in this value are replaced as follows: * ENDPOINT: The last segment (following `endpoints/`)of the Endpoint.name][] field of the Endpoint where this Model has been deployed. (Vertex AI makes this value available to your container code as the [`AIP_ENDPOINT_ID` environment variable](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#aip-variables).) * DEPLOYED_MODEL: DeployedModel.id of the `DeployedModel`. (Vertex AI makes this value available to your container code as the [`AIP_DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID` environment variable](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#aip-variables).)

For example, the following example sets the variable `VAR_2` to have the value `foo bar`: ```json [ { "name": "VAR_1", "value": "foo" }, { "name": "VAR_2", "value": "$(VAR_1) bar" } ] ``` If you switch the order of the variables in the example, then the expansion does not occur. At most 200 environment variables can be specified. Each variable (`NAME=value`) must be smaller than 128 KiB, and the total size of all variables must not exceed 512 KiB.

args.description: Immutable. Specifies arguments for the command that runs when the container starts. This overrides the container's [`CMD`](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#cmd). Specify this field as an array of executable and arguments, similar to a Docker `CMD`'s "default parameters" form. If you don't specify this field but do specify the command field, then the command from the `command` field runs without any additional arguments. See the [Kubernetes documentation about how the `command` and `args` fields interact with a container's `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/inject-data-application/define-command-argument-container/#notes). If you don't specify this field and don't specify the `command` field, then the container's [`ENTRYPOINT`](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#cmd) and `CMD` determine what runs based on their default behavior. See the Docker documentation about [how `CMD` and `ENTRYPOINT` interact](https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/builder/#understand-how-cmd-and-entrypoint-interact). In this field, you can reference [environment variables set by Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/custom-container-requirements#aip-variables) and environment variables set in the env field. You cannot reference environment variables set in the Docker image. In order for environment variables to be expanded, reference them by using the following syntax: $( VARIABLE_NAME) Note that this differs from Bash variable expansion, which does not use parentheses. If a variable cannot be resolved, the reference in the input string is used unchanged. To avoid variable expansion, you can escape this syntax with `$$`; for example: $$(VARIABLE_NAME) This field corresponds to the `args` field of the Kubernetes Containers [v1 core API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.23/#container-v1-core).

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1StudySpecCon.description: Configuration for ConvexAutomatedStoppingSpec. When there are enough completed trials (configured by min_measurement_count), for pending trials with enough measurements and steps, the policy first computes an overestimate of the objective value at max_num_steps according to the slope of the incomplete objective value curve. No prediction can be made if the curve is completely flat. If the overestimation is worse than the best objective value of the completed trials, this pending trial will be early-stopped, but a last measurement will be added to the pending trial with max_num_steps and predicted objective value from the autoregression model.

minStepCount.description: Minimum number of steps for a trial to complete. Trials which do not have a measurement with step_count > min_step_count won't be considered for early stopping. It's ok to set it to 0, and a trial can be early stopped at any stage. By default, min_step_count is set to be one-tenth of the max_step_count. When use_elapsed_duration is true, this field is set to the minimum elapsed seconds.

maxStepCount.description: Steps used in predicting the final objective for early stopped trials. In general, it's set to be the same as the defined steps in training / tuning. If not defined, it will learn it from the completed trials. When use_steps is false, this field is set to the maximum elapsed seconds.

useElapsedDuration.description: This bool determines whether or not the rule is applied based on elapsed_secs or steps. If use_elapsed_duration==false, the early stopping decision is made according to the predicted objective values according to the target steps. If use_elapsed_duration==true, elapsed_secs is used instead of steps. Also, in this case, the parameters max_num_steps and min_num_steps are overloaded to contain max_elapsed_seconds and min_elapsed_seconds.

learningRateParameterName.description: The hyper-parameter name used in the tuning job that stands for learning rate. Leave it blank if learning rate is not in a parameter in tuning. The learning_rate is used to estimate the objective value of the ongoing trial.

minMeasurementCount.description: The minimal number of measurements in a Trial. Early-stopping checks will not trigger if less than min_measurement_count+1 completed trials or pending trials with less than min_measurement_count measurements. If not defined, the default value is 5.

updateAllStoppedTrials.description: ConvexAutomatedStoppingSpec by default only updates the trials that needs to be early stopped using a newly trained auto-regressive model. When this flag is set to True, all stopped trials from the beginning are potentially updated in terms of their `final_measurement`. Also, note that the training logic of autoregressive models is different in this case. Enabling this option has shown better results and this may be the default option in the future.

GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1Verifier.description: A declarative success criterion for a goal. Harness-agnostic: the runtime follows the description to decide pass/fail and to repair on failure. A criterion may be checked automatically (`auto_verification`, `nl_criteria`, `command_check`) or by a human (`human_check`, resolved via a HITL elicitation at verification time). If `kind` is unset the Verifier carries no criterion and is ignored. On a Task with a local environment, verifiers do not access the environment: `nl_criteria` and `auto_verification` are judged on the record of the agent's work in the current turn, and `command_check` is not allowed.

enumDescriptions: Default value. This value is unused.
No verdict yet, or the verifier awaits a person.
Failed an attempt; the agent is still working on the goal this turn.
Passed. Final until the client replaces the goal's spec, which puts the verifier back to `PENDING`. Verdicts judged on the old spec are not applied once the new spec has been sent to the agent.
Failed with no attempts left this turn. Unless the goal is then `FAILED`, the next turn judges it again.
The client removed this verifier. It stays in `Goal.verifiers` so later verifiers keep their index, and it is no longer judged.

disableMemory.description: Optional. If true, the agent neither reads existing memories into the prompt nor forms new ones from this task. Memory is on by default, and this can only turn it off, never back on: * Agent memory enabled, this true: off for this task. * Agent memory enabled, this false or unset: on. * Agent memory disabled: off, whatever this says. Because a task belongs to a single end user's interaction, a surface that knows the user can use this to turn memory off for one user of a shared agent; memory keeps working for the agent's other users. `Agent.memory_config.disable_memory` wins because it is the mutable one. It can be turned on after tasks have already been created, and a stored task spec keeps whatever it was created with — so if a spec could re-enable memory, the agent-level switch would be unable to cover the tasks that already exist. The two are therefore OR'ed, and the agent's current value is re-applied every time a session opens, including on a resume. Scoped to this task. Memories already stored for the agent are retained and stay readable by the agent's users; this governs only whether this task can access and modify them.

biasSlices.description: Specification for how the data should be sliced for bias. It contains a list of slices, with limitation of two slices. The first slice of data will be the slice_a. The second slice in the list (slice_b) will be compared against the first slice. If only a single slice is provided, then slice_a will be compared against "not slice_a". Below are examples with feature "education" with value "low", "medium", "high" in the dataset: Example 1: bias_slices = [{'education': 'low'}] A single slice provided. In this case, slice_a is the collection of data with 'education' equals 'low', and slice_b is the collection of data with 'education' equals 'medium' or 'high'. Example 2: bias_slices = [{'education': 'low'}, {'education': 'high'}] Two slices provided. In this case, slice_a is the collection of data with 'education' equals 'low', and slice_b is the collection of data with 'education' equals 'high'.

budgetMilliNodeHours.description: The training budget of creating this model, expressed in milli node hours i.e. 1,000 value in this field means 1 node hour. The actual metadata.costMilliNodeHours will be equal or less than this value. If further model training ceases to provide any improvements, it will stop without using the full budget and the metadata.successfulStopReason will be `model-converged`. Note, node_hour = actual_hour * number_of_nodes_involved. For modelType `cloud`(default), the budget must be between 8,000 and 800,000 milli node hours, inclusive. The default value is 192,000 which represents one day in wall time, considering 8 nodes are used. GoogleCloudAiplatformV1beta1TaskServerEv.description: A single Server -> Client event. There is intentionally no non-terminal error/notice branch. Transient, retriable failures (tool-fetch retry, rate-limit, scheduler retry) are handled by runtime retry (bounded by TaskSpec.max_retries) and, if surfaced at all, appear as trajectory steps; the terminal error is reported once via TaskCompletedEvent.outcome.status (google.rpc.Status). This follows the Interactions events.proto, which deprecated its dedicated non-terminal InteractionPausedEvent and reports terminal status on InteractionCompletedEvent.

stepDelta.description: One chunk of a streamed step, carrying only the content generated since the previous chunk. Chunks sharing an `index` belong to one step and concatenate in the order received.

stepStart.description: Opens a streamed step. Emitted only under `TaskSpec.delta_streaming`, which documents the two delivery modes in full. Under `delta_streaming` EVERY step arrives as a `step_start` / `step_delta`* / `step_stop` run sharing an `index`, and a bare `step` is never emitted. Reassembling a run yields the same Step that `step` above would otherwise have delivered. What follows a `step_start` depends on whether the content is generated progressively. Assistant text (and the citations on it) and thoughts stream across the run's `step_delta`s as they are produced, so for those this field carries the step's shape (role, type) with its generated content left empty. A step that arrives whole -- tool calls, tool results, elicitations, user-input echoes, errors -- carries no `step_delta` at all: the COMPLETE step rides this field, and `step_stop` closes the run.

continuationToken.description: Optional. Opaque resume cursor covering everything delivered through this event, inclusive. A client that keeps the token from the last event it processed and passes it back on SubscribeTaskEvent.continuation_token or StreamTaskRequest.continuation_token resumes at the next event, with no gap and no duplicate. Opaque: the encoding is a server implementation detail and may change without notice. Do not parse it, compare two of them, or derive ordering from it -- order by `seq_num`. Carries no task id, because every RPC that redeems a token already names the task it applies to. It is a position, not a capability: it grants no access on its own, and the task's IAM check is what authorizes the read. This is the resume cursor. Resuming by number (next_step_seq_num on SubscribeTaskEvent and StreamTaskRequest) is slated for deprecation: a number cannot address a position inside a streamed step, while the token can, so a reconnect mid-answer does not re-send the part of that answer the client already rendered. `seq_num` remains for ordering only.

seqNum.description: Required. 1-based, non-decreasing sequence number within the server direction, stable across reconnects, so it can be used to resume: a given event carries the same number however the stream is (re)connected. Gapless on a stream delivered from the beginning. Clients acknowledge receipt via ack_output_seq_num and resume via SubscribeTaskEvent.next_step_seq_num. A resume with next_step_seq_num = 0 (or unset) restarts from the first still available step. A number identifies a resume point, not an event, so it is not unique: consecutive events can share one. An event derived from another (an artifacts_changed delta carrying the plan its step just wrote) repeats its source's number rather than taking the next, which keeps the numbering a function of the stream alone and guarantees a cursor never lands between the two. Acknowledging a number acknowledges every event carrying it. A resume can begin AFTER the requested number. next_step_seq_num counts events, but a streamed step spans several of them, so a cursor can point inside a run; the server then suppresses that run's remaining step_delta/step_stop rather than deliver frames for a step the client never saw opened, and resumes at the next step boundary. Numbering is unchanged by that suppression -- keeping it stable is what makes a cursor meaningful across connections -- so the first delivered event may be a later number than asked for. Treat the sequence as monotonic, not densely contiguous, when resuming.

statusChanged.description: A coarse status transition (e.g. WORKING -> REQUIRES_ACTION when the task is waiting on a human response).

eventId.description: Optional. The TaskClientEvent.event_id this event was derived from, echoed back verbatim. Set only on the events that carry a client input back out: the `step` echoing the input, and the `step_start` of a streamed step the input opened. Empty everywhere else -- on model-generated steps the server produced on its own, on the step_delta/step_stop frames continuing a run (correlate those by `index` with their step_start), and on any event whose client input carried no event_id. Purely a correlation handle: it does not order or acknowledge anything, and the server never derives behavior from it. Since the server does not enforce uniqueness, a client that reuses an id sees it on every echo it produced. Delivered to every client subscribed to the task, not just the one that sent the input, including on a later replay from storage.

step.description: A trajectory output step (thought, tool call, content, elicitation_call, etc.). Human-in-the-loop requests are just steps: the server emits an ElicitationCallStep (for an approval / choice) or a ToolCallStep (for a client-executed tool), and the client responds with the matching ElicitationResultStep / ToolResultStep, correlated by elicitation_id / call_id. The kind of action required is inferred from the step's type, so there is no separate "action required" event.

timestampMicros.description: Strictly increasing generation timestamp, in unix micros.

stepUsage.description: Optional. Token usage for one model call. Populated on at most one event per model call regardless of `TaskSpec.delta_streaming`, and absent on non-model events (tool results, user-input echoes, status changes).

trajectoryId.description: Optional. The runtime trajectory UUID that produced this event's step, e.g. "e9df8df3-d63a-4747-ad00-eaef837d7d31". A debugging correlation handle and the join key to the runtime's per-step trajectory record (for Sobi, the Trajectory Store viewer at sobi.corp.google.com/trajectory/). Set on the step-bearing events (`step` and the `step_start` of a streamed step); empty on status_changed / artifacts_changed and on the step_delta/step_stop frames continuing a run (correlate those by `index` with their step_start). Also empty on steps the Sobi converter did not build: the actor delivers `elicitation_call` as a native `Step` payload with no field 110, and `Session::ReadConverted` forwards it unchanged (`jetski_to_interaction_stream_converter.cc:1101-1104`), so a HITL turn reaches the client on `step` with `trajectory_id` empty even though a trajectory does exist for it. A whole turn shares one trajectory id. The server never derives behavior from it. See b/552010818.

agentResource.description: Required. Immutable. The name of the agent that the OnlineEvaluator evaluates periodically. stateDetails.description: Output only. Contains additional information about the state of the OnlineEvaluator. This is used to provide more details in the event of a failure.

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the OnlineEvaluator was created.

enumDescriptions: Default value.
Indicates that the OnlineEvaluator is active.
Indicates that the OnlineEvaluator is suspended. In this state, the OnlineEvaluator will not evaluate any samples.
Indicates that the OnlineEvaluator is in a failed state. This can happen if, for example, the `log_view` or `trace_view` set on the `CloudObservability` does not exist.

Indicates that the OnlineEvaluator is in a warning state. This can happen if, for example, some of the metrics in the `metric_sources` are invalid. Evaluation will still run with the remaining valid metrics.
state.description: Output only. The state of the OnlineEvaluator.

cloudObservability.description: Data source for the OnlineEvaluator, based on Google Cloud Observability stack (Cloud Trace & Cloud Logging).

references.description: References for the given prompt. The key is the name of the reference, and the value is the reference itself. Users can use this field together with the reward configurations to calculate rewards for reinforcement tuning. For example, users can set the following references: ``` { "concise_answer": "Yes", "verbose_answer": "The answer is Yes" } ``` Then in a ReinforcementTuningCodeExecutionRewardScorer reward function config, for example, they can define a python code snippet as follows: ``` def evaluate(example, response) -> float: response_str = response.get("parts", [])0 references = example.get("references", {}) if response_str == references.get("concise_answer"): return 1.0 return -1.0 ``` In this case, references can serve the purpose of holding the ground truth of this example in the training/validation dataset.

Supported fields (any other field yields INVALID_ARGUMENT): * `latest_detection_time` - the session's most-recent flagged detection time. `latest_detection_time desc` puts the newest sessions first. * `max_severity_rank` - the session's bucketed maximum severity, ranked LOW=1 < MEDIUM=2 < HIGH=3 < CRITICAL=4. `max_severity_rank desc` puts the most-severe sessions first. * `agent_display_name` - the MonitoredAgent's display name. Sorted as a STRING (case-sensitive, code-point order). If empty, defaults to `latest_detection_time desc`. Multi-field sort (for example, `max_severity_rank desc, latest_detection_time desc`) is supported. The `order_by` value MUST match the value used on the call that minted any supplied `page_token` (AIP-158). Mismatches yield INVALID_ARGUMENT.

filter.description: Optional. Filter expression restricting which AnalyzedSessions are returned. Supports a subset of AIP-160: a closed `detection_time` window (both bounds required), an equality on `severity`, an equality on `agent_type`, and an equality on `session_id`, joined by `AND`. Each clause is optional, may appear at most once, and may appear in any order. The `severity` value is the **canonical** `Severity` enum name -- `SEVERITY_CRITICAL`, `SEVERITY_HIGH`, `SEVERITY_MEDIUM` or `SEVERITY_LOW`. Short forms such as `"CRITICAL"` are rejected, as is `SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED`. It matches sessions whose *maximum* severity equals that bucket: a session that fires at both LOW and CRITICAL matches `severity = "SEVERITY_CRITICAL"`, not `severity = "SEVERITY_LOW"`. The `agent_type` value is the canonical `AgentResource.AgentType` enum name -- `REASONING_ENGINE`, `CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE`, `GKE_WORKLOAD`, `GCE_INSTANCE`, `AGENT_TYPE_OTHER` or `AGENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` -- and matches sessions run by an agent on that runtime. Unlike `severity`, `agent_type` accepts its `UNSPECIFIED` value. The two are not analogous: a session always has a computed severity bucket, so `SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED` is never returned and filtering on it could only match nothing. `AGENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` *is* returned -- it is what `AnalyzedSession.agent_type` reports for an agent whose runtime was never recorded -- so it must remain filterable. The `session_id` value is a case-sensitive exact match (no substring or prefix matching) on `AnalyzedSession.session_id`. Unlike `severity` and `agent_type` it is not a closed enum, so any non-empty value is accepted; an empty value (`session_id = ""`) is rejected rather than treated as "no filter". Example (time window, severity and runtime): ``` detection_time >= "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" AND detection_time <= "2024-01-08T00:00:00Z" AND severity = "SEVERITY_CRITICAL" AND agent_type = "CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE" ``` If empty, results are restricted to the last 7 days with no severity, runtime, or session restriction. Other fields, additional operators, set membership (`IN`), and boolean combinations (`OR`, `NOT`, parentheses) are not yet supported.

filter.description: Optional. A filter expression, e.g. "status=WORKING". Lineage filters pick how much of a task tree to fetch: * "parent_task_id=" -- direct children only (progressive disclosure, one level per call). * "root_task_id=" -- the whole tree in one flat collection. Label filters support filtering by task labels: * "labels.=" -- match tasks with the given label key and value. Multiple label filters can be combined with AND. Multiple values for the same key can be combined with OR, e.g., "labels.foo=bar OR labels.foo=baz". Status filters restrict the listing to tasks in the given statuses: * "status=" -- e.g. "status=WORKING". Multiple statuses can be combined with OR, e.g., "status=WORKING OR status=IDLE". Both page normally via `page_size`/`page_token`, and both are ordered by `order_by` (default "create_time desc"), not by tree shape. A whole-tree page is therefore not a subtree: a child can arrive before its parent, so the client buffers by `parent_task_id` and renders as parents resolve.

Characters that are not one of alphanumeric `[a-zA-Z0-9]`, underscore `_`, or asterisk `*` are treated as delimiters for tokens. `*` is treated as a wildcard that matches characters within a token. * Ignoring case. * Prepending an asterisk to the first and appending an asterisk to the last token in QUERY. A QUERY must be either a singular token or a phrase. A phrase is one or multiple words enclosed in double quotation marks ("). With phrases, the order of the words is important. Words in the phrase must be matching in order and consecutively. Supported FIELDs for field-restricted queries: * `feature_id` * `description` * `entity_type_id` Examples: * `feature_id: foo` --> Matches a Feature with ID containing the substring `foo` (eg. `foo`, `foofeature`, `barfoo`). * `feature_id: foo*feature` --> Matches a Feature with ID containing the substring `foo*feature` (eg. `foobarfeature`). * `feature_id: foo AND description: bar` --> Matches a Feature with ID containing the substring `foo` and description containing the substring `bar`. Besides field queries, the following exact-match filters are supported. The exact-match filters do not support wildcards. Unlike field-restricted queries, exact-match filters are case-sensitive. * `feature_id`: Supports = comparisons. * `description`: Supports = comparisons. Multi-token filters should be enclosed in quotes. * `entity_type_id`: Supports = comparisons. * `value_type`: Supports = and != comparisons. * `labels`: Supports key-value equality as well as key presence. * `featurestore_id`: Supports = comparisons. Examples: * `description = "foo bar"` --> Any Feature with description exactly equal to `foo bar` * `value_type = DOUBLE` --> Features whose type is DOUBLE. * `labels.active = yes AND labels.env = prod` --> Features having both (active: yes) and (env: prod) labels. * `labels.env: *` --> Any Feature which has a label with `env` as the key.

add.description: Adds a file, folder or site stored in Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint or another third-party store as an artifact. The service persists `link_json_metadata` to Cloud Storage as a JSON metadata reference (a `.link.json` file), and links it to a parent resource: a task, named by `task`, or a collaborative project, named by `collaborative_project`. This method is idempotent with respect to the linked entity, identified by `link_json_metadata.provider` and `link_json_metadata.source_artifact_id`, or `link_json_metadata.uri` when `source_artifact_id` is unset: adding an entity that the parent already has does not add another artifact, and returns the same `artifact_id`.

remove.description: Deletes a file from a task's workspace. `path` must be an absolute path to a file in the task's workspace, under `/workspace/`, e.g. `/workspace/userdata/input.csv`. A path outside `/workspace/`, including a relative path, or a path with a `..` segment fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A directory path, or a task in a terminal state, fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A missing file fails with `NOT_FOUND` unless `allow_missing` is `true`, in which case the call succeeds and changes nothing.

path.description: Required. Absolute path of a file in the task's workspace, e.g. `/workspace/report.pptx`, or, for a collaborative project, under `/workspace/project`, e.g. `/workspace/project/report.pptx`. Must be under `/workspace`, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Accepts `TaskArtifactFile.path` as-is.

preview.description: Returns a file converted for a preview, such as a PDF of a .pptx. A server-streaming RPC. A PDF asked for as a PDF is returned as stored. Fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` when the file cannot be converted (an unsupported format, too large, or unreadable), with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` when the conversion takes too long, and with `UNAVAILABLE` when conversion is busy or not available; the last two may succeed on a retry.

filter.description: Optional. An AIP-160 filter expression that entries must match, e.g. `type = FILE AND mime_type = "image/*"`. Empty matches every entry. Supported fields: * `type` -- `FILE` or `DIRECTORY` (see `TaskArtifactFile.Type`), case-sensitive. * `mime_type` -- a media type in double quotes, e.g. `"text/csv"`. `*` is a wildcard, so `"image/*"` matches every image type. Directories have an empty `mime_type`. Comparisons use `=` or `!=` and combine with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (or `-`) and parentheses. A filter that is not valid AIP-160, or that uses another field or operator, is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The filter selects which entries are returned, not which directories are walked: with `recursive`, `type = FILE` still returns the files in subdirectories.

parent.description: Required. The task or collaborative project whose workspace to list. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

path.description: Optional. Absolute path of the directory to list, e.g. `/workspace/userdata`. Must be `/workspace` or under it, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Defaults to `/workspace`.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous ListWorkspaceArtifacts call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page. When paginating, all other fields of the request except `page_size` must match the call that provided the page token. The workspace is live: the agent can write between pages, so a paged listing is not a snapshot. An entry added during the walk may or may not appear, and one removed may still be listed and then fail to download.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of entries to return. The service may return fewer than this value, including none on a page that is not the last. If unspecified or 0, at most 100 are returned. The maximum is 1000; values above 1000 are coerced to 1000. A negative value is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

recursive.description: Optional. If `true`, descends into subdirectories. Results are breadth-first.

list.description: Lists the files and directories in a task's workspace. By default only the immediate children of `path` are returned; set `recursive` to descend into subdirectories. Entries that match `filter` are returned in breadth-first order. While the task's sandbox is running, paths it writes locally are read from the sandbox so the listing reflects files not yet synced to storage; otherwise they are read from storage. Which one served a request is not visible to the caller.

create.description: Creates a task without opening a live channel. Convenient for scheduled/background tasks where the caller does not need to drive the execution interactively; observe progress later via StreamTask (or by reconnecting to CreateTaskBidiStream with a `subscribe_task` request).

userContext.channel.description: Optional. How the user's input reached the agent. Leave unset when the user talks to the agent directly in an AI-native interface.
enumDescriptions: Default. The user is talking to the agent directly in an AI-native interface (e.g. the Gemini Enterprise app, Workspace Studio, or the Gemini app), or the channel is unknown. The agent applies no channel-specific behavior.

A threaded conversation on a communication product where the agent is one participant, e.g. a Google Chat DM or space, or a comment thread on a document. The agent keeps its reply short and conversational, suited to a thread that others can read, and may ask a follow-up question.
An email message. The agent writes a complete, self-contained reply suited to email, and avoids follow-up questions it could anticipate, since each round trip is slow.

userContext.location.description: Optional. The user's coarse, human-readable location, e.g. "Mountain View, CA, US". Must be no more precise than city level; never send street addresses, postal codes, or coordinates. The agent uses it for location-dependent requests, e.g. weather or nearby places.

uniqueCreationToken.description: Optional. Optional idempotency token to guarantee the task is created only once. Suggest a UUID. A create carrying a token that a live task of the same agent already holds fails with `ALREADY_EXISTS`, naming that task in the response. The token is free again once that task finishes.

userContext.timeZone.description: Optional. The user's IANA time zone name, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". The agent uses it to interpret and present dates and times, e.g. to resolve "tomorrow morning".

path.description: Required. Absolute path of the file to read, e.g. "/workspace/report.md". Must be under "/workspace", at most 1024 characters, and not contain a ".." segment.

processingConfig.outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type to return: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. a .docx or .pptx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid. Any other value fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

task.description: Required. The task to download from. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

downloadArtifact.description: Downloads a file from a task's workspace as a stream of chunks. A server-streaming RPC. The response body is the file's raw bytes, with the file's own media type as the `Content-Type`. At most 1 GiB. Like ListTaskArtifacts, reads from the running sandbox when there is one, so a file the agent has just written is returned even before it reaches storage.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of tasks to return. The service may return fewer. If unspecified (or <= 0), at most 50 are returned. The maximum is 100; larger values are capped to 100.

parent.description: Required. The parent to list tasks under. Both forms are accepted and scope the listing differently: * projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent} -- tasks assigned to that agent. * projects/{project}/locations/{location} -- all tasks in the location.

filter.description: Optional. A filter expression, e.g. "status=WORKING". Lineage filters pick how much of a task tree to fetch: * "parent_task_id=" -- direct children only (progressive disclosure, one level per call). * "root_task_id=" -- the whole tree in one flat collection. Label filters support filtering by task labels: * "labels.=" -- match tasks with the given label key and value. Multiple label filters can be combined with AND. Multiple values for the same key can be combined with OR, e.g., "labels.foo=bar OR labels.foo=baz". Status filters restrict the listing to tasks in the given statuses: * "status=" -- e.g. "status=WORKING". Multiple statuses can be combined with OR, e.g., "status=WORKING OR status=IDLE". Both page normally via `page_size`/`page_token`, and both are ordered by `order_by` (default "create_time desc"), not by tree shape. A whole-tree page is therefore not a subtree: a child can arrive before its parent, so the client buffers by `parent_task_id` and renders as parents resolve.

orderBy.description: Optional. Sort order, e.g. "create_time desc". The sortable fields are `create_time` and `update_time`. Defaults to "create_time desc".

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token from a previous ListTasks call.

list.description: Lists tasks under a parent. Supports filtering (e.g. by status or assigned_agent) so a surface can show "my tasks".

path.description: Required. Absolute path of a file in the task's workspace, e.g. `/workspace/report.md`, or, for a collaborative project, under `/workspace/project`, e.g. `/workspace/project/report.md`. Must be under `/workspace`, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Accepts `TaskArtifactFile.path` as-is.

processingConfig.outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type of the rendition: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. of a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx or .csv, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid. Any other value fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

name.description: Required. The task or collaborative project to download from. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

download.description: Downloads a file. The response body is the file's bytes, with the file's own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` that names the file. Media is the default and only representation, so no `alt` parameter is needed. A preview sets `processing_config` and gets a rendition of the file in place of the file, such as a PDF of a .pptx: the response body is the rendition, with its own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` name that ends in its extension. Without `processing_config` the response is always the stored file.

suspend.description: Suspends a task, pausing its active turn or scheduling loop and transitioning the status to SUSPENDED. The underlying runtime session remains resumable.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to suspend. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

nextStepSeqNum.description: Optional. The next step sequence number to resume from. When zero, streams from the beginning of the available trajectory.

snapshot.description: Optional. If true, streams only the events produced up to the current point in time and terminates the stream once all existing events are sent, rather than tailing and waiting for future events.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to stream. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

continuationToken.description: Optional. Opaque resume cursor, as issued on TaskServerEvent.continuation_token. Replay continues immediately after the event that carried the token. Takes precedence over next_step_seq_num when both are set. A token this stream cannot redeem is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than silently falling back to the numeric cursor, so a client cannot mistake a rejected resume for a replay from the start; reconnect without a token instead. That covers a malformed token, one issued by a connection whose delta streaming differs from this one's (see TaskSpec.delta_streaming), one issued while the server derived task status differently, and any token on a recurring task. A token names a position in the task it was issued on; send it only to that task. It carries no task id, so a token from another task is not rejected, and what it returns is undefined. A token whose position is past the events stored so far is not an error either, because storage can trail the live stream that issued the token: the replay skips everything up to that position, so a snapshot may return no events.

stream.description: Read-only server-stream of a task's execution by id: trajectory steps and status changes, resumable from a step sequence number. Unlike CreateTaskBidiStream, it does not accept client inputs -- use it to observe or replay a task (the trajectory is not stored on the Task resource). This is the entry point for *observers*: it tails the trajectory from interaction storage without restoring the runtime actor, so it adds no restore latency and continues to follow output that a participant driving the task on a CreateTaskBidiStream connection produces. Observe-only clients should prefer this over a subscribe_task connect on CreateTaskBidiStream, which restores the actor and is meant for clients that will send input.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to retrieve. Both name forms are accepted: * projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} * projects/{project}/locations/{location}/tasks/{task}

get.description: Gets a task.

deleteArtifact.description: Deletes a file from a task's workspace. `path` must be an absolute path to a file under `/workspace/userdata/` (for example, `/workspace/userdata/input.csv`). Paths outside `/workspace/userdata/`, `/workspace/userdata` itself, relative paths, or paths with `.` or `..` segments fail with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Directory paths and tasks in a terminal state fail with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A missing file fails with `NOT_FOUND` unless `allow_missing` is true, in which case the call succeeds with an empty response.

task.description: Required. The task to delete from. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

cancel.description: Deprecated: use `CancelTaskLro` instead. This method keeps the same cancellation semantics but returns `Task` directly, which forecloses the future cascade behaviour on recurring parents that only an `Operation` return type can express. Cancels a task, out-of-band by id. Drains any in-progress work and moves the task to CANCELLED. Use this when there is no active stream (e.g. a scheduled or background task) or when a caller other than the streaming client cancels. A task may also be cancelled in-band via the bidi cancel_task end_request; the two paths are equivalent. Cancellation semantics: * Idempotent: cancelling an already-terminal task is a no-op that returns the current Task; concurrent/duplicate cancels collapse to one CANCELLED. * First terminal state wins: once the task is CANCELLED/COMPLETED/FAILED, later cancels have no effect. * Cancel takes precedence over complete_task: a cancel arriving while (or after) a client half-closes with complete_task still drives the task to CANCELLED rather than letting it finish.

name.description: Required. The name of the task to cancel. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}
Required. The name of the task to delete. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

operateOnSelf.description: Optional. Whether to skip cascading deletion to all descendant subtasks. Defaults to false (cascades to all descendants by default). Matches google.cloud.aiplatform.master.CancelTaskRequest.operate_on_self. Behavior: UNSET or false ⇒ cascade: delete this task and every non-terminal descendant (gated by Mendel flag sobi_enable_cascading_delete_task; returns FAILED_PRECONDITION when the flag is OFF and the task has non-terminal children). true ⇒ delete this task only. Each descendant deletion signals the runtime for the live-session case (Actor.OnCancel finalizes trajectory + reclaims sandbox VM) before removing the Sobi DB rows, matching the single-DeleteTask contract.

delete.description: Deletes a task. Long-running because deletion cascades: it cancels any active run (WORKING / REQUIRES_ACTION / SUSPENDED tasks are cancelled-then-deleted, not rejected), and cleans up the task's bound resources -- environment, generated artifacts, and the runtime trajectory/sessions. The operation completes when the cascade finishes; on success the response is google.protobuf.Empty.

name.description: Required. The task or collaborative project to upload to. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

upload.description: Uploads a file. The task must not be in a terminal state, and an existing file at `path` is replaced. At most 10 GiB.

task.description: Required. The task to upload into. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

path.description: Required. Absolute destination path, e.g. "/workspace/userdata/input.csv". Must be under "/workspace/userdata/" and at most 1024 characters; relative paths and paths containing a ".." segment are rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

uploadArtifact.description: Uploads a file into a task's workspace. A client-streaming RPC: the request body is the file's raw bytes, relayed to storage a chunk at a time, so neither ESF nor this server holds the whole file. A broken connection restarts the upload from zero. `path` must be an absolute path under `/workspace/userdata/`. The task must not be in a terminal state. An existing file at `path` is replaced. At most 1 GiB.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token from a previous ListTaskArtifacts call. The workspace is live: the agent can write between pages, so a paged listing is not a snapshot. An entry added during the walk may or may not appear, and one removed may still be listed and then fail to download.

recursive.description: Optional. If true, descends into subdirectories. Results are breadth-first.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of entries to return. The service may return fewer. If unspecified (or <= 0), at most 100 are returned. The maximum is 1000; larger values are capped to 1000.

task.description: Required. The task whose workspace to list. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task}

path.description: Optional. Absolute path of the directory to list, e.g. "/workspace/userdata". Must be "/workspace" or under it, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a ".." segment. Defaults to "/workspace".

listArtifacts.description: Lists the files in a task's workspace. By default only the immediate children of `path` are returned; set `recursive` to descend into subdirectories. Entries are returned in breadth-first order. While the task's sandbox is running, paths it writes locally are read from the sandbox so the listing reflects files not yet synced to storage; otherwise they are read from storage. Which one served a request is not visible to the caller.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of agents to return. The service may return fewer than this value. The maximum page size is 100; values above 100 will be coerced to 100. If unspecified, the default page size is 10.

orderBy.description: Optional. A comma-separated list of fields to order by. Supported fields: * `created` * `updated` Use `desc` after a field name for descending order. Example: `created desc`.

parent.description: Required. The resource name of the location to list agents from. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}`.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous AgentService.ListAgents call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page.

filter.description: Optional. An [AIP-160](https://google.aip.dev/160) filter over the returned agents. An empty filter returns the unfiltered collection. Supported fields, and the operators each accepts: * `created` * `updated` * `base_agent` * `metadata.agent_type` `created` and `updated` are timestamps and take an RFC-3339 value, for example `2026-08-01T00:00:00Z`. Supported operators: `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `:`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (equivalently `-`), and parentheses. Note that `OR` binds more tightly than `AND`, so `a AND b OR c` means `a AND (b OR c)`; parentheses are recommended, not required. `metadata.agent_type` accepts only the value `"default_agent"`, matched exactly: `metadata.agent_type:"default_agent"` selects the caller's default agent, of which there is at most one, and the negated form selects the rest. Any other value is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` rather than an empty page -- `metadata` is an opaque blob, so only this one marker is indexed, and the server cannot answer a question about the others. An agent designated before the server began recording the marker is not matched by the positive form; there is no backfill. `base_agent` accepts `=` and `!=` against the value an agent was created with, and selects only among the agents you own: an agent that belongs to the project rather than to a user is never returned by a filter naming it, including the negated form. An agent created before the server began recording the value is not matched either. Example: `created > "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z" AND updated < "2026-08-09T00:00:00Z"`. IMPORTANT -- `base_agent` and `metadata.agent_type` select only among the agents you own. An agent that belongs to the project rather than to a user is never returned by a filter naming either of them, including a negated one: `base_agent != "some-value"` returns your matching agents and no project-owned agents at all. Filtering on `created` or `updated` alone is unaffected and still spans both. If you want every agent in the project, do not filter on these two fields. Not supported: any field other than those listed above, wildcards other than `field:*`, bare literals with no field name, functions, and the regular-expression operators `=~` and `!~`. A filter that names an unsupported field, exceeds 1000 characters, or nests parentheses more than 5 deep fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

list.description: Lists the agents in a location that belong to the caller. An agent belongs to the end user recorded as its owner when it was created, so the response holds that caller's agents and no others. It is empty for a caller that is not an end user, and an agent with no recorded owner is listed for nobody.

testIamPermissions.description: Returns permissions that a caller has on the specified resource. If the resource does not exist, this will return an empty set of permissions, not a `NOT_FOUND` error. Note: This operation is designed to be used for building permission-aware UIs and command-line tools, not for authorization checking. This operation may "fail open" without warning.

permissions.description: The set of permissions to check for the `resource`. Permissions with wildcards (such as `*` or `storage.*`) are not allowed. For more information see [IAM Overview](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/overview#permissions).

REQUIRED: The resource for which the policy is being specified. See [Resource names](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/resource_names) for the appropriate value for this field.

options.requestedPolicyVersion.description: Optional. The maximum policy version that will be used to format the policy. Valid values are 0, 1, and 3. Requests specifying an invalid value will be rejected. Requests for policies with any conditional role bindings must specify version 3. Policies with no conditional role bindings may specify any valid value or leave the field unset. The policy in the response might use the policy version that you specified, or it might use a lower policy version. For example, if you specify version 3, but the policy has no conditional role bindings, the response uses version 1. To learn which resources support conditions in their IAM policies, see the [IAM documentation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/help/conditions/resource-policies).

Resources the agent owns but a caller never named -- its AI Application and the tenant project bound to it, its Workspace identity, its service-extension binding -- are torn down with the agent on every delete, whatever this field says.

orderBy.description: A comma-separated list of fields to order by. The default sort order is in ascending order. Use "desc" after a field name for descending. You can have multiple order_by fields provided. For example, using "create_time desc, end_time" will order results by create time in descending order, and if there are multiple schedules having the same create time, order them by the end time in ascending order. If order_by is not specified, it will order by default with create_time in descending order. Supported fields: * `create_time` * `start_time` * `end_time` * `next_run_time`

The following fields are supported: * `display_name`: Supports `=`, `!=` comparisons, and `:` wildcard. * `state`: Supports `=` and `!=` comparisons. * `request`: Supports existence of the check. (e.g. `create_pipeline_job_request:*` --> Schedule has create_pipeline_job_request). * `create_time`: Supports `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` comparisons. Values must be in RFC 3339 format. * `start_time`: Supports `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` comparisons. Values must be in RFC 3339 format. * `end_time`: Supports `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` comparisons and `:*` existence check. Values must be in RFC 3339 format. * `next_run_time`: Supports `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` comparisons. Values must be in RFC 3339 format. Filter expressions can be combined together using logical operators (`NOT`, `AND` & `OR`). The syntax to define filter expression is based on https://google.aip.dev/160. Examples: * `state="ACTIVE" AND display_name:"my_schedule_*"` * `NOT display_name="my_schedule"` * `create_time>"2021-05-18T00:00:00Z"` * `end_time>"2021-05-18T00:00:00Z" OR NOT end_time:*` * `create_pipeline_job_request:*`

wait.description: Waits until the specified long-running operation is done or reaches at most a specified timeout, returning the latest state. If the operation is already done, the latest state is immediately returned. If the timeout specified is greater than the default HTTP/RPC timeout, the HTTP/RPC timeout is used. If the server does not support this method, it returns `google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`. Note that this method is on a best-effort basis. cancel.description: Starts asynchronous cancellation on a long-running operation. The server makes a best effort to cancel the operation, but success is not guaranteed. preview.description: Returns a file converted for a preview, such as a PDF of a .pptx. A server-streaming RPC. The response body is the converted file's bytes, with its media type as the `Content-Type`. The server converts the file as it is stored now, on every call, and stores nothing. A PDF asked for as a PDF is returned as stored. Fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` when the file cannot be converted (an unsupported format, too large, or unreadable), with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` when the conversion takes too long, and with `UNAVAILABLE` when conversion is busy or not available; the last two may succeed on a retry.

outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type to convert the file to: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. of a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx or .csv, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid.

path.description: Required. Absolute path of a file in the task's workspace, e.g. `/workspace/report.pptx`, or, for a collaborative project, under `/workspace/project`, e.g. `/workspace/project/report.pptx`. Must be under `/workspace`, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Accepts `TaskArtifactFile.path` as-is.

parent.description: Required. The task or collaborative project whose workspace holds the file. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

add.description: Adds a file, folder or site stored in Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint or another third-party store as an artifact. The service persists `link_json_metadata` to Cloud Storage as a JSON metadata reference (a `.link.json` file), and links it to a parent resource: a task, named by `task`, or a collaborative project, named by `collaborative_project`. This method is idempotent with respect to the linked entity, identified by `link_json_metadata.provider` and `link_json_metadata.source_artifact_id`, or `link_json_metadata.uri` when `source_artifact_id` is unset: adding an entity that the parent already has does not add another artifact, and returns the same `artifact_id`.

collaborativeProject.description: Optional. The collaborative project to link the file to. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project} Exactly one of `task` and `collaborative_project` must be set.

remove.description: Deletes a file from a task's workspace. `path` must be an absolute path to a file in the task's workspace, under `/workspace/`, e.g. `/workspace/userdata/input.csv`. A path outside `/workspace/`, including a relative path, or a path with a `..` segment fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A directory path, or a task in a terminal state, fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A missing file fails with `NOT_FOUND` unless `allow_missing` is `true`, in which case the call succeeds and changes nothing.

parent.description: Required. The task or collaborative project whose workspace holds the file. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

list.description: Lists the files and directories in a task's workspace. By default only the immediate children of `path` are returned; set `recursive` to descend into subdirectories. Entries that match `filter` are returned in breadth-first order. While the task's sandbox is running, paths it writes locally are read from the sandbox so the listing reflects files not yet synced to storage; otherwise they are read from storage. Which one served a request is not visible to the caller.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of entries to return. The service may return fewer than this value, including none on a page that is not the last. If unspecified or 0, at most 100 are returned. The maximum is 1000; values above 1000 are coerced to 1000. A negative value is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

filter.description: Optional. An AIP-160 filter expression that entries must match, e.g. `type = FILE AND mime_type = "image/*"`. Empty matches every entry. Supported fields: * `type` -- `FILE` or `DIRECTORY` (see `TaskArtifactFile.Type`), case-sensitive. * `mime_type` -- a media type in double quotes, e.g. `"text/csv"`. `*` is a wildcard, so `"image/*"` matches every image type. Directories have an empty `mime_type`. Comparisons use `=` or `!=` and combine with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (or `-`) and parentheses. A filter that is not valid AIP-160, or that uses another field or operator, is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The filter selects which entries are returned, not which directories are walked: with `recursive`, `type = FILE` still returns the files in subdirectories.

recursive.description: Optional. If `true`, descends into subdirectories. Results are breadth-first.

path.description: Optional. Absolute path of the directory to list, e.g. `/workspace/userdata`. Must be `/workspace` or under it, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Defaults to `/workspace`.

parent.description: Required. The task or collaborative project whose workspace to list. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}/tasks/{task} or projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collaborativeProjects/{collaborative_project}

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous ListWorkspaceArtifacts call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page. When paginating, all other fields of the request except `page_size` must match the call that provided the page token. The workspace is live: the agent can write between pages, so a paged listing is not a snapshot. An entry added during the walk may or may not appear, and one removed may still be listed and then fail to download.

The following fields are supported: * `pipeline_name`: Supports `=` and `!=` comparisons. * `display_name`: Supports `=`, `!=` comparisons, and `:` wildcard. * `pipeline_job_user_id`: Supports `=`, `!=` comparisons, and `:` wildcard. for example, can check if pipeline's display_name contains *step* by doing display_name:\"*step*\" * `state`: Supports `=` and `!=` comparisons. * `create_time`: Supports `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` comparisons. Values must be in RFC 3339 format. * `update_time`: Supports `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` comparisons. Values must be in RFC 3339 format. * `end_time`: Supports `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=` comparisons. Values must be in RFC 3339 format. * `labels`: Supports key-value equality and key presence. * `template_uri`: Supports `=`, `!=` comparisons, and `:` wildcard. * `template_metadata.version`: Supports `=`, `!=` comparisons, and `:` wildcard. Filter expressions can be combined together using logical operators (`AND` & `OR`). For example: `pipeline_name="test" AND create_time>"2020-05-18T13:30:00Z"`. The syntax to define filter expression is based on https://google.aip.dev/160. Examples: * `create_time>"2021-05-18T00:00:00Z" OR update_time>"2020-05-18T00:00:00Z"` PipelineJobs created or updated after 2020-05-18 00:00:00 UTC. * `labels.env = "prod"` PipelineJobs with label "env" set to "prod".

download.description: Downloads a file. The response body is the file's bytes, with the file's own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` that names the file. Media is the default and only representation, so no `alt` parameter is needed. A preview sets `processing_config` and gets a rendition of the file in place of the file, such as a PDF of a .pptx: the response body is the rendition, with its own media type as the `Content-Type` and a `Content-Disposition` name that ends in its extension. Without `processing_config` the response is always the stored file.

processingConfig.outputMimeType.description: Required. The media type of the rendition: * `application/pdf`: the file as a PDF, e.g. of a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx. * `application/json`: a spreadsheet, e.g. a .xlsx or .csv, as JSON describing its sheets and cells, from which a client draws the workbook as a grid. Any other value fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

Must be under `/workspace`, at most 1024 characters, and not contain a `..` segment. Accepts `TaskArtifactFile.path` as-is.

It may return the latest state before the specified timeout (including immediately), meaning even an immediate response is no guarantee that the operation is done.
